import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 8.29

by L. A. Kurdachenko

Do there exist locally nilpotent groups with trivial centre satisfying the weak maximal
condition for normal subgroups?

A group is *locally nilpotent* if every finitely generated subgroup is nilpotent. A group
satisfies the *weak maximal condition for normal subgroups* (Baer's condition
$\mathrm{Max}\text{-}\infty\text{-}n$) if it has no infinite strictly ascending chain
$N_1 < N_2 < \cdots$ of normal subgroups in which every index $|N_{i+1} : N_i|$ is infinite.
Equivalently, in every ascending chain of normal subgroups all but finitely many of the
indices $|N_{i+1} : N_i|$ are finite. This is weaker than the maximal condition for normal
subgroups $\mathrm{Max}\text{-}n$ (the ascending chain condition on normal subgroups).

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«8.29»

/-- A group `G` is locally nilpotent if every finitely generated subgroup of `G` is nilpotent. -/
def IsLocallyNilpotent (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ H : Subgroup G, H.FG → Group.IsNilpotent H

/-- A group `G` satisfies the weak maximal condition for normal subgroups (Baer's condition
$\mathrm{Max}\text{-}\infty\text{-}n$) if there is no infinite strictly ascending chain
$N_0 < N_1 < N_2 < \cdots$ of normal subgroups of `G` in which every index $|N_{i+1} : N_i|$
is infinite.

Here `(N i).relIndex (N (i + 1))` is the index of `N i` in `N (i + 1)`, and `Subgroup.relIndex`
returns `0` exactly when this index is infinite. -/
def WeakMaxNormal (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ¬ ∃ N : ℕ → Subgroup G,
    (∀ i, (N i).Normal) ∧ StrictMono N ∧ ∀ i, (N i).relIndex (N (i + 1)) = 0

/-- A nilpotent group is locally nilpotent. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsLocallyNilpotent.of_isNilpotent (G : Type*) [Group G] [Group.IsNilpotent G] :
    IsLocallyNilpotent G :=
  fun _ _ => inferInstance

/-- A finite group satisfies the weak maximal condition for normal subgroups. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem WeakMaxNormal.of_finite (G : Type*) [Group G] [Finite G] : WeakMaxNormal G :=
  fun ⟨_, _, _, h⟩ => Subgroup.index_ne_zero_of_finite (h 0)

/--
Do there exist locally nilpotent groups with trivial centre satisfying the weak maximal
condition for normal subgroups?

The group is required to be nontrivial, since the trivial group vacuously satisfies all
three conditions.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«8.29» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ (G : Type) (_ : Group G), Nontrivial G ∧ IsLocallyNilpotent G ∧
      Subgroup.center G = ⊥ ∧ WeakMaxNormal G := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«8.29»
attempts.decomposition_objections: None. The single-slot decomposition and its notes (nontriviality required; weak Max-n ≠ Max-n) match my reading of the statement.
modeling_decisions: Weak maximal condition formalized in the 'no bad chain' form (no strictly ascending ℕ-indexed chain of normal subgroups with every consecutive index infinite), which is Baer's/Robinson's literal definition; the equivalent 'eventually finite-index steps' form is mentioned in the module docstring but not used.

`StrictMono N` is included for literal faithfulness to 'N₁ < N₂ < ⋯'; it is in fact implied by the infinite-index condition (equal consecutive terms would have relIndex 1, not 0), so it is harmless redundancy.
Infinite index is expressed as `Subgroup.relIndex … = 0`, relying on Mathlib's convention that `relIndex` returns 0 exactly for infinite index; this is documented in the definition's docstring.
The group is quantified over `Type` (universe 0), following the existing Kourovka files (e.g. 1_74.lean).
`Nontrivial G` is added to exclude the trivial group, which would otherwise make the existential trivially true; this is explained in the theorem docstring.

Two short fully-proved `@[category API]` tests (`IsLocallyNilpotent.of_isNilpotent`, `WeakMaxNormal.of_finite`) are included to exercise the bespoke definitions, per the repository's 'add basic API tests' guideline; the bespoke definitions are kept in the problem file (as in Kourovka/1_40.lean) since the task restricts writing to the candidate file.

/-!
# Conjecture 8.29

by L. A. Kurdachenko

maximal condition for normal subgroups?

chain $N_1 < N_2 < \cdots$ of normal subgroups in which every index $|N_{i+1} : N_i|$

$\mathrm{Max}\text{-}n$, which forbids all infinite strictly ascending chains of normal subgroups.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«8.29»

/-- A group is locally nilpotent if every finitely generated subgroup is nilpotent. -/
def IsLocallyNilpotent (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ H : Subgroup G, H.FG → Group.IsNilpotent H

/-- A group $G$ satisfies the weak maximal condition for normal subgroups if there is no
infinite strictly ascending chain $N_0 < N_1 < N_2 < \cdots$ of normal subgroups of $G$ such
that every index $|N_{i+1} : N_i|$ is infinite.

Here `(N i).relIndex (N (i + 1))` is the index of `N i` in `N (i + 1)`, and `Subgroup.relIndex`
is `0` exactly when this index is infinite. -/
def WeakMaxNormal (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ¬ ∃ N : ℕ → Subgroup G,
    (∀ i, (N i).Normal) ∧ (∀ i, N i < N (i + 1)) ∧ (∀ i, (N i).relIndex (N (i + 1)) = 0)

/-- Every nilpotent group is locally nilpotent. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsLocallyNilpotent.of_isNilpotent (G : Type*) [Group G] [Group.IsNilpotent G] :
    IsLocallyNilpotent G :=
  fun _ _ => inferInstance

/-- A group satisfying the maximal condition for normal subgroups (no infinite strictly
ascending chain of normal subgroups at all) satisfies the weak maximal condition for normal
subgroups. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem WeakMaxNormal.of_forall_not_strictMono (G : Type*) [Group G]
    (h : ∀ N : ℕ → Subgroup G, (∀ i, (N i).Normal) → ¬ StrictMono N) :
    WeakMaxNormal G := by
  rintro ⟨N, hN, hlt, -⟩
  exact h N hN (strictMono_nat_of_lt_succ hlt)

/-- The trivial group is a locally nilpotent group with trivial centre satisfying the weak maximal
condition for normal subgroups. This is why the problem asks for a nontrivial group. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem trivial_group_satisfies_conditions :
    IsLocallyNilpotent Unit ∧ Subgroup.center Unit = ⊥ ∧ WeakMaxNormal Unit := by
  refine ⟨IsLocallyNilpotent.of_isNilpotent Unit, Subsingleton.elim _ _, ?_⟩
  rintro ⟨N, -, hlt, -⟩
  exact (hlt 0).ne (Subsingleton.elim _ _)

/--
Do there exist locally nilpotent groups with trivial centre satisfying the weak maximal
condition for normal subgroups?

That is: is there a nontrivial group $G$ such that every finitely generated subgroup of $G$ is
nilpotent, $Z(G) = 1$, and $G$ has no infinite strictly ascending chain $N_1 < N_2 < \cdots$
of normal subgroups with all indices $|N_{i+1} : N_i|$ infinite?

The trivial group satisfies all three conditions vacuously, so it is excluded.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«8.29» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ (G : Type) (_ : Group G), Nontrivial G ∧ IsLocallyNilpotent G ∧
      Subgroup.center G = ⊥ ∧ WeakMaxNormal G := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«8.29»

Chains are indexed by ℕ (ω-chains), which is the standard meaning of 'ascending chain' in Max-∞-n.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 8.29

by L. A. Kurdachenko

Do there exist locally nilpotent groups with trivial centre satisfying the weak
maximal condition for normal subgroups?

A group is *locally nilpotent* if every finitely generated subgroup is nilpotent.
A group satisfies the *weak maximal condition for normal subgroups* (Baer's
condition $\mathrm{Max}$-$\infty$-$n$) if it has no infinite strictly ascending
chain $N_0 < N_1 < N_2 < \cdots$ of normal subgroups in which every index
$|N_{i+1} : N_i|$ is infinite. Equivalently, in every ascending chain of normal
subgroups all but finitely many of the indices $|N_{i+1} : N_i|$ are finite.
This is weaker than the ordinary maximal condition for normal subgroups.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«8.29»

variable (G : Type*) [Group G]

/-- A group $G$ is *locally nilpotent* if every finitely generated subgroup of $G$ is
nilpotent. -/
def IsLocallyNilpotent : Prop :=
  ∀ H : Subgroup G, H.FG → Group.IsNilpotent H

/-- A group $G$ satisfies the *weak maximal condition for normal subgroups*
(Baer's condition $\mathrm{Max}$-$\infty$-$n$) if there is no infinite strictly
ascending chain $N_0 < N_1 < N_2 < \cdots$ of normal subgroups of $G$ in which every
index $|N_{i+1} : N_i|$ is infinite.

Here `(N n).relIndex (N (n + 1))` is the index of $N_n$ in $N_{n+1}$, and
`Subgroup.relIndex` returns `0` exactly when this index is infinite. -/
def WeakMaxNormal : Prop :=
  ¬ ∃ N : ℕ → Subgroup G, (∀ n, (N n).Normal) ∧ StrictMono N ∧
    ∀ n, (N n).relIndex (N (n + 1)) = 0

/--
Do there exist locally nilpotent groups with trivial centre satisfying the weak
maximal condition for normal subgroups?

The trivial group is excluded explicitly: it is locally nilpotent, has trivial
centre, and satisfies the weak maximal condition for normal subgroups, so without
`Nontrivial G` the question would have a vacuous positive answer.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«8.29» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ (G : Type) (_ : Group G), Nontrivial G ∧ IsLocallyNilpotent G ∧
      Subgroup.center G = ⊥ ∧ WeakMaxNormal G := by
  sorry

-- Sanity checks

/-- A nilpotent group is locally nilpotent. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsLocallyNilpotent.of_isNilpotent [Group.IsNilpotent G] : IsLocallyNilpotent G :=
  fun _ _ => inferInstance

/-- A finite group satisfies the weak maximal condition for normal subgroups. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem WeakMaxNormal.of_finite [Finite G] : WeakMaxNormal G :=
  fun ⟨N, _, hN, _⟩ => not_injective_infinite_finite N hN.injective

/-- The trivial group satisfies all three conditions of the problem. This is why the
problem statement requires `Nontrivial G`. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
example : IsLocallyNilpotent Unit ∧ Subgroup.center Unit = ⊥ ∧ WeakMaxNormal Unit :=
  ⟨IsLocallyNilpotent.of_isNilpotent Unit, Subsingleton.elim _ _, WeakMaxNormal.of_finite Unit⟩

end Kourovka.«8.29»
